q: 1. 'Loess' is silty clay formed by the action of
explain: Loess is a uniform, fine-grained (silt-sized) deposit laid down by wind (aeolian action) over long periods.

q: 2. Pick up the correct sequence of geological cycle for the formation of soil
explain: The geological cycle of soil formation consists of weathering of parent rock, transportation of particles, deposition in a new location, and eventual upheaval.

q: 3. Which of the following is a glacial soil?
options: Deposited at the bottom of the lakes
explain: Glacial soils are transported and deposited directly by glacier ice, which none of the other options (river, lake, sea) describe.

q: 4. 'Drift' is the material picked up, mixed, disintegrated, transported and re-deposited by
explain: Drift refers to all material transported and deposited by glaciers, either directly by moving ice or by the meltwater (glacier water) flowing from it.

q: 5. Talus is the soil transported by .............
explain: Talus is scree that accumulates at the base of a slope or cliff due to gravity-driven rockfall.

q: 6. Non-cohesive soil is
explain: Sand consists of coarse, bulky grains with negligible inter-particle attraction, so it has no cohesion, unlike clay/silt which show cohesive behaviour.

q: 7. Physical weathering occurs due to
explain: Physical or mechanical weathering breaks rocks into smaller fragments without changing their chemical composition, often via temperature shifts or mechanical force.

q: 8. The soil transported by flowing water is called
explain: Soil carried and deposited by rivers/streams (flowing water) is termed alluvial soil.

q: 9. Agent of transportation for alluvial soils is .............
explain: Alluvial soils are transported and deposited by flowing water such as rivers.

q: 10. Lacustrine soils are those which are
options: deposited at the bottom of lakes
deposited due to moving of ice sheets
explain: 'Lacustrine' derives from Latin 'lacus' (lake); these soils settle out of still water at lake bottoms.

q: 11. Honey combed structure is found in
explain: Honeycombed structures are typical of fine-grained soils like fine silts where particles settle and form large voids.

q: 12. Soils are basically
explain: Soil is a complex mixture containing inorganic mineral particles as well as organic matter from decomposed organisms.

q: 13. Cohesionless soil is
explain: Sands are considered cohesionless because their particles do not stick together; their strength comes from internal friction.

q: 14. The behaviour of silt is normally governed by
explain: Silt particles are intermediate in size; their behavior is influenced by both gravitational (mass) forces and surface electrical forces.

q: 15. Residual soils are
explain: Residual soils form in place by weathering of parent rock and can occur as sand, silt or clay depending on rock type and weathering degree — hence all of these.

q: 16. Who is the father of Geotechnical Engineering?
explain: Karl von Terzaghi is universally acknowledged as the father of both soil mechanics and geotechnical engineering.

q: 17. Shape of clay particles is .............
explain: Clay minerals commonly form flaky or needle-like (acicular) particle shapes due to their sheet-silicate crystal structure.

q: 18. Honey combed structure is found in
explain: Honeycomb structure (an open, arch-like arrangement of grains) is typically formed in fine silts and fine sands due to inter-particle bonding during sedimentation.

q: 19. Which is the correct definition of soil in geotechnical engineer's point of view?
options: Soil is the top surface of the earth where plants can grow
Soil is the unconsolidated material consisting particles produced by disintegration of rock which may or may not contain organic matter
Soil is the relatively thin surface zone which can contain moisture
explain: Geotechnically, soil is defined as unconsolidated mineral/rock-derived particles, which may or may not contain organic matter, distinct from the agricultural definition.

q: 20. Chemical weathering of soil is caused due to
explain: Chemical weathering of parent rock into soil occurs through multiple processes — oxidation, carbonation, and hydration — all contributing to mineral breakdown.

q: 21. Chemical weathering occurs because of .............
explain: Oxidation, carbonation, and hydration are all chemical processes that break down rock minerals, contributing to chemical weathering.

q: 22. Black cotton soil
options: Contains low percentage of clay minerals
explain: Black cotton soil is characteristically dark grey to black in colour, due to its montmorillonite clay content and organic staining, though it is inorganic in origin.

q: 23. The depth of exploration for square footing should be at least .............
explain: For an isolated square footing, exploration should extend to about twice the footing width to capture the significant stressed zone.

q: 24. The depth of exploration of a strip footing should be at least .............
explain: For strip footings, exploration depth of about twice the footing width is recommended to capture the stress-influenced zone.

q: 25. The soil transported by water and deposited along the stream is called
explain: Alluvial soil is specifically the material carried and deposited by flowing river/stream water along its course.

q: 26. Pile foundation are suitable for
explain: Piles are primarily used to transfer structural loads down through weak upper soil layers to a firm, competent bearing stratum below (end-bearing piles).

q: 27. Well foundations in sandy soils derive their bearing capacity from
explain: In cohesionless sandy strata, well foundations rely mainly on point (end) bearing resistance at the base rather than skin friction along the shaft.

q: 28. Agent responsible for the transportation of soil is
explain: Soil transportation and deposition can occur via wind (aeolian), water (alluvial/lacustrine/marine), or gravity (talus/colluvial) — all are recognized transporting agents.

q: 29. Which of the following soils will have least value of safe load?
explain: Soft chalk is the weakest and most compressible of these materials, giving it the lowest safe bearing load.

q: 30. The soil transported by running water is called .............
explain: Soil transported and deposited by flowing rivers/streams is classified as alluvial soil.

q: 31. Caissons are structures used for
options: Dewatering while laying foundations in proper position
explain: Caissons are large prefabricated box/well structures sunk into the ground/water to allow foundations to be constructed properly in position, especially below water or through soft strata.

q: 32. The soil transported by wind is called .............
explain: Wind-transported and deposited soil is termed aeolian soil (e.g., loess, dune sand).

q: 33. Stability number is given by
explain: Per Taylor's stability chart formulation, the dimensionless stability number is expressed as Sn = C²/H in this book's given equation form.

q: 34. Generally hand augers are used when the depth is about .............
explain: Hand augers are a simple manual tool practical only for shallow exploration, typically up to about 6 m depth.

q: 35. Lacustrine soils are those soils which are .............
options: deposited at the bottom of the lakes
explain: Lacustrine soils are, by definition, transported by water and deposited at the bottom of lakes.

q: 36. Shallow footing is one whose depth is
explain: Per Terzaghi's definition, a shallow foundation has depth less than or equal to (approximately) its width, not strictly less than, more than, or always equal — hence 'none of the above' as per the book's answer.

q: 37. Glacial soils are those soils which are .............
options: deposited at the bottom of the lakes
explain: Glacial soils are transported and deposited directly by glacier ice, which none of the given options describe.

q: 38. Value of factor of safety adopted in foundation design is
explain: For bearing capacity calculations in foundation design, a factor of safety in the range of 2.5 to 3.0 is conventionally adopted to account for uncertainties.

q: 39. Mode of transportation for alluvial soils is generally
explain: By definition, alluvial soils are those transported and deposited by the action of flowing water (rivers/streams).

q: 40. Cohesionless soils are formed due to
options: Leaching action of water on rocks
Blowing of cold and hot wind
explain: Cohesionless (granular) soils like sand and gravel primarily result from mechanical/physical disintegration of parent rock (weathering by temperature change, abrasion, freeze-thaw), not chemical alteration.

q: 41. Generally soil refers to .............
explain: Per the reference key soil is described as a solid medium, referring to its mineral solid framework.

q: 42. An agent responsible for the transportation of soil is .............
explain: Per the reference key wind is marked as the answer; note that water and gravity are also recognized transportation agents, so 'all of the above' is the commonly expected textbook answer.

q: 43. If the soil stays at a place above the parent rock where it is produced, then it is called .............
explain: Soil that remains in place above its parent rock, without transportation, is classified as residual soil.

q: 44. Physical weathering occurs due to .............
explain: Physical (mechanical) weathering results from thermal expansion/contraction, ice wedging, and root action, all acting together.

q: 45. Bore holes are found to be economical than the test pits when the depth of exploration is around .............
explain: Beyond about 6 m depth, boring becomes more economical than excavating open test pits, which get costly and unstable at greater depth.

q: 46. For making holes in hard strata the preferred one is .............
explain: Percussion drilling, which pulverizes hard material by repeated impact, is preferred for penetrating hard strata.

q: 47. A raft foundation is preferred for .............
options: load bearing walls of multistoreyed buildings
columns of a building which are closely spaced
explain: When columns are closely spaced (individual footings would overlap), a raft foundation combines them into one continuous slab.

q: 48. For engineering purposes, soil is defined as .............
options: the loose mantle at the surface of the earth which favours the growth of plant
a natural aggregate of mineral grains, loose or moderately cohesive, inorganic or organic in nature
explain: The engineering definition of soil is a natural aggregate of mineral grains that are loose or moderately cohesive, unlike the agricultural definition tied to plant growth.

q: 49. Soils are derived from .............
explain: Soil can form from the weathering of any rock type — igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.

q: 50. Chemical weathering of soil is caused due to .............
explain: Chemical weathering results from oxidation, hydration, carbonation, and leaching acting together on rock minerals.
